case_name: M. P. Oil Extraction v State of Madhya Pradesh and Others
facts: The case involves three special leave petitions filed by M.P. Oil Extraction Ltd. and K.N. Oil Industries against the Madhya Pradesh High Court's judgment dated 9.5.1995.
Before the said writ petitions were filed, a series of litigations were fought between the parties to these appeals both in the Madhya Pradesh High Court and in this Court.
The appellants had set up their first solvent extraction plant in 1966 using bran rice as raw material.
The Industrial Policy laid down by the M.P. Government in 1977 envisaged supply of sal seeds to the new units as well as to the existing old units.
The said Industrial Policy also laid down that new units should be encouraged to set up their plants with concessions during the initial period for a period of 5 to 10 years.
issues: Whether the State Government's agreements with Bastar Oil Mills and Sal Udyog (Pvt.) Ltd. are violative of Articles 14 and 19 of the Constitution of India.
Whether the State Government has acted malafide in treating only few of the industrial units of the State in a very favoured manner by entering into fresh agreements for supply of sal seeds.
petitioner_arguments: The appellants had set up their first solvent extraction plant in 1966 using bran rice as raw material.
The Industrial Policy laid down by the M.P. Government in 1977 envisaged supply of sal seeds to the new units as well as to the existing old units.

The State Government being fully aware of the availability of sal seeds in 1991 which was a meagre 19809 M.T. acted malafide in treating only few of the industrial units of the State in a very favoured manner by entering into fresh agreements for supply of 50,000 M.T. of sal seeds to the new units.
respondent_arguments: The respondents Bastar Oil Mills and Sal Udyog (Pvt.) Ltd. had been receiving a large quantity of sal seeds from the State Government.
The State Government has acted in a fair and reasonable manner by entering into agreements with the respondents for supply of sal seeds.
court_reasoning: The Court held that the State Government's agreements with Bastar Oil Mills and Sal Udyog (Pvt.) Ltd. are violative of Articles 14 and 19 of the Constitution of India.

The Court observed that the State Government has acted malafide in treating only few of the industrial units of the State in a very favoured manner by entering into fresh agreements for supply of sal seeds.
holding: The Court allowed the appeals and quashed the agreements between the State Government and Bastar Oil Mills and Sal Udyog (Pvt.) Ltd. for supply of sal seeds.
The Court directed the State Government to distribute the surplus sal seeds among all the industrial units operating in the State, including the appellants.
